newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin fines Harvard C&C for trading deals.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin fines Harvard C&C for trading deals.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry fined Czech-based fund manager Harvard Capital & Consulting (HC&C) the maximum one million crowns and forced it to pay compensation for various illegal trading activities, a senior ministry official said on Monday.
"(Harvard) had several violations of the law on investment companies and funds," Marie Jezkova, the head of the ministry's department of fund supervision department, told Reuters.

She said Harvard, founded by Czech-born entreprenuer Viktor Kozeny and not connected with the U.S. college where he once studied, was fined for the manipulation of assets of a publicly-held closed-end investment fund which Harvard managed, the Harvard Guarantee and Multiple Fund.
She said that the violations included "dealing with the assets of the fund with unprofessional care".
Numerous attempts by Reuters to reach Harvard officials for comment were fruitless.
Jezkova said that Harvard conducted trades which "did not indicate that they were done with the aim to increase the value of the assets of the fund".
She was reacting to repeated inquiries to the ministry concerning a story published last week in the U.S. magazine Fortune.
The magazine quoted a still unpublished ministry decision taken in July to fine Harvard one million crowns and force it to pay $6.8 million in compensation to its funds for various activities.

Jezkova declined comment on the total amount of compensation Harvard was required to pay, but she said that the ministry did impose the maximum fine allowable by law, and that Harvard did have to pay additional compensation.
